items.stem: Distinguish between 'personal troubles' and 'public issues'.
items.answer: Personal troubles: problems that an individual experiences in his or her own life, such as losing a job. Public issues: problems that affect many people and arise from the structure of society, such as large-scale unemployment.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 for explaining 'personal troubles' (problems that an individual experiences in his or her own life, such as losing a job.) and 1 for 'public issues' (problems that affect many people and arise from the structure of society, such as large-scale unemployment.), with the contrast made clear.

items.stem: Name Weber's three types of authority with an example of each.
items.answer: Traditional (hereditary chief, king); charismatic (leader with extraordinary qualities); rational-legal (bureaucrat, elected government).
items.markingKey: 2 marks: Traditional (hereditary chief, king); charismatic (leader with extraordinary qualities); rational-legal (bureaucrat, elected government).

items.stem: Give a reason for the following: Class is called an open system of stratification.

items.stem: State the census criteria for an urban area in India.
items.answer: Minimum population of 5,000; density of at least 400 persons per sq km; at least 75 per cent of male workers in non-agricultural occupations.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: Minimum population of 5,000; density of at least 400 persons per sq km; at least 75 per cent of male workers in non-agricultural occupations.

items.stem: What is cultural lag? Give an example.
items.answer: When non-material culture (values, norms) changes more slowly than material culture (technology); e.g., norms on mobile phone or internet use lagging behind technology.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: When non-material culture (values, norms) changes more slowly than material culture (technology); e.g., norms on mobile phone or internet use lagging behind technology.

items.stem: Distinguish between 'Fordism' and 'scientific management'.
items.answer: Fordism: a system of mass production on assembly lines, named after Henry Ford's car factories. Scientific management: Frederick Taylor's method of breaking work into simple, timed tasks to raise output, also called Taylorism.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 for explaining 'Fordism' (a system of mass production on assembly lines, named after Henry Ford's car factories.) and 1 for 'scientific management' (Frederick Taylor's method of breaking work into simple, timed tasks to raise output, also called Taylorism.), with the contrast made clear.

items.stem: Distinguish between 'segmental division' and 'hierarchical division'.
items.answer: Segmental division: Ghurye's first feature of caste, by which society is divided into closed groups with membership by birth. Hierarchical division: Ghurye's feature of caste by which castes are ranked from highest to lowest in purity and status.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 for explaining 'segmental division' (Ghurye's first feature of caste, by which society is divided into closed groups with membership by birth.) and 1 for 'hierarchical division' (Ghurye's feature of caste by which castes are ranked from highest to lowest in purity and status.), with the contrast made clear.

items.stem: How did the Industrial Revolution influence the rise of sociology?

items.markingKey: 2 marks: Factories, urbanisation and new working conditions; poverty and social problems; time discipline; need for surveys; questions about how society is held together.

items.stem: Distinguish between mechanical and organic solidarity.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the scope of sociology and its relationship with other social sciences and answer the questions that follow.
"Social anthropology traditionally studied small, simple societies, but its methods are now used to study modern societies too. Economics traditionally focused on the production, distribution and consumption of goods, while sociology sees economic behaviour in its social context. Sociology studies the interconnections between different parts of social life."
(i) Which discipline traditionally studied the past, while sociology focused on contemporary society? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'social psychology' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Sociologists study economic behaviour in a social context. (2)
items.answer: (i) History (ii) The field that links psychology and sociology by studying the individual in a social setting. (iii) Economic activity is shaped by norms, values, institutions and social relationships.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) History (ii) The field that links psychology and sociology by studying the individual in a social setting. (iii) Economic activity is shaped by norms, values, institutions and social relationships.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"Bureaucracy is a feature of modern society based on rational-legal authority. In a bureaucracy, officials work within fixed areas of jurisdiction with written rules and files. An ideal type is not an average or a perfect model but an analytical tool for comparison. Weber identified traditional, charismatic and rational-legal authority."
(i) Explain the term 'rational-legal authority', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Weber advocated empathetic understanding. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "An ideal type means the best or perfect example of something." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) Authority based on legal rules and impersonal procedures, characteristic of bureaucracy. (ii) Social action has subjective meaning for the actor, which the sociologist must grasp. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It is an analytical model highlighting key features, not a perfect model.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) Authority based on legal rules and impersonal procedures, characteristic of bureaucracy. (ii) Social action has subjective meaning for the actor, which the sociologist must grasp. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It is an analytical model highlighting key features, not a perfect model.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on Émile Durkheim on the division of labour, solidarity and social facts and answer the questions that follow.
"Durkheim used the study of law as an indicator of the type of solidarity in a society. In societies with organic solidarity, individuals are different but depend on each other. In societies with mechanical solidarity, individuals are similar and bound by shared beliefs."
(i) Durkheim said social facts should be studied as: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'restitutive law' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Durkheim called social facts 'things'. (2)
items.answer: (i) things (ii) Law that aims to repair the harm done, as found in societies with organic solidarity. (iii) They are external to individuals and can be studied objectively like natural phenomena.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) things (ii) Law that aims to repair the harm done, as found in societies with organic solidarity. (iii) They are external to individuals and can be studied objectively like natural phenomena.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"According to D.P. Mukerji, the three principles of change in Indian tradition were shruti, smriti and anubhava. D.P. Mukerji held that Indian culture and society were not individualistic but group-oriented. D.P. Mukerji regarded personal and collective experience as the main source of change in Indian tradition. D.P. Mukerji felt that the Indian middle classes educated in Western ways were cut off from their own traditions."
(i) Explain the term 'shruti', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: D.P. Mukerji stressed the study of traditions. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "D.P. Mukerji considered smriti the revolutionary principle of change." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) That which is heard; one of the principles of change in Indian tradition according to D.P. Mukerji. (ii) Indian society was group-oriented and its culture was shaped by inherited traditions. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: He considered anubhava (experience) the revolutionary principle.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) That which is heard; one of the principles of change in Indian tradition according to D.P. Mukerji. (ii) Indian society was group-oriented and its culture was shaped by inherited traditions. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: He considered anubhava (experience) the revolutionary principle.

items.stem: Distinguish between 'urbanisation' and 'gated community'.
items.answer: Urbanisation: the growth of towns and cities and the increase in the proportion of the population living in them. Gated community: an enclosed residential area with controlled entry, built by the well-off for security and exclusivity.
